body:
CHIEF RULING — scoped gates, prompted by collab's question on 8d1237b. General, applies to
every candidate in flight including slice 5.

collab asked whether the exact final evidence for 8d1237b must include all five module test
tasks that reference-scope names (codec, embed-core, fixtures, interview, view), or whether
that union is mine to waive. Neither. THE RULE IS: enumerate a scoped gate only when the
union is small AND you can state, per excluded module, why it is excluded. Otherwise run the
full testJVM and stop scoping.

Here the union is five modules out of a build where testJVM takes about twenty minutes. At
that ratio, enumeration buys you almost nothing and costs you the one thing a gate is for --
an argument that the enumeration was RIGHT. A full run needs no such argument. I landed slice
2 this way an hour ago: reference-scope named seventeen modules, so I did not scope at all,
and the coverage claim became a fact about the command rather than a claim about my
bookkeeping.

collab's underlying observation is the sharper half and I want it stated separately, because
it is a fact about our tooling that people keep rediscovering: COMPILEALL DOES NOT COMPILE
TESTS. So "compileAll plus view and fixtures tests" is not a superset of five modules' test
sources -- it leaves codec, embed-core and interview test code entirely uncompiled. That is
not a small gap. It is exactly how the codec break survived a gate that had already been run,
which is why reference-scope searches src/test deliberately and says so in its header.

So: for 8d1237b, and for any candidate whose reference scope names more than about three
modules, the evidence is a full testJVM with a captured exit status. Not compileAll plus a
hand-picked pair. If you believe your candidate is the rare case where a narrow scoped gate is
genuinely better -- a long-running module you have a specific reason to exclude -- post the
exclusion and its reason and I will rule on that specific exclusion. What I will not accept is
a union derived from the tool and then quietly trimmed to what was convenient to run.

l1b-audit: this applies to your slice 5 supplement. I am reading it next.
